label: mcl_core_leaves_birch
reference_prompt: Create a close visual reference for birch foliage in a cool grounded dark-fantasy woodland. Birch leaves should feel lighter, thinner and more restless than oak: many small delicate leaves with fine serrated character, layered loosely enough for air and pale light to move through the canopy. Weather introduces muted yellow-green variation, tiny browned edges and occasional curled or damaged leaves. Use restrained fresh-to-olive green rather than deep jungle tones. Avoid oversized leaves, dense hedge masses, autumn-yellow dominance, ornamental garden cleanliness or photographic botanical isolation. The reference should communicate birch's quick, airy canopy and cool-climate fragility while still belonging to the same aged, tactile world. Do not design a repeating leaf pattern.
